title: Sr. Security Operations Manager
description: About Carrot: Carrot is the leading global fertility and family care platform, built on intelligent care orchestration: the right clinical guidance, at the right moment, in the context of each memberâs life. More than a thousand multinational employers, health plans, and health systems trust Carrot to support millions of members across 195 countries â from pre-pregnancy through menopause and major life moments in between. Carrot's comprehensive clinical program delivers industry-leading cost savings for plan sponsors and award-winning experiences and improved outcomes for millions of people worldwide. Carrot is widely regarded as a defining force in healthcare innovation as a recipient of several top-tier awards, including Fast Company's 'Most Innovative Companies' and CNBC's '100 Barrier Breaking Startups'. The company is regularly cited by leading global outlets â including The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, NPR, ABC News, and Harvard Business Review â as a leading voice on digital health, the future of work, and family health. Learn more at get-carrot.com . The Opportunity ð Carrot is looking for a senior, hands-on security leader to run our security operations and help set the direction for how we adopt AI safely in this space. In this player-coach role, you will own how we detect, investigate, and respond to threats, and you will secure the corporate and AI tools our employees rely on every day. You will build where it has the most impact: detection logic, automation, and AI agents that allow a small team to operate at scale. AI runs through this role. Our teams work across collaboration platforms, enterprise search, workflow automation, AI assistants, and custom agents connected to internal systems, and each one changes how sensitive data moves. You will make sure we adopt these tools quickly and safely, and you will use AI to automate as much of the security pipeline as possible. Much of this job happens between teams. You will partner with IT, Legal, Privacy, and Engineering, and you will get partner teams to meet security commitments through influence rather than authority. As part of the Information Security team, you will also contribute to privacy, vendor risk, compliance, and customer assurance in a healthcare environment. Â What Youâll Own ð¼ In this role, you will: Own the security incident lifecycle, from intake and triage through containment, communication, and post-incident review. Act as incident commander, run tabletop exercises, and coordinate with Legal and Privacy on breach notification. Manage our managed security provider: hold them to SLAs, own escalation and handoffs, and tune what they alert on so alerts turn into action. Revisit what stays outsourced as our automation matures. Own our detection and investigation program in our SIEM. Build detections and AI-assisted investigations that scale without pulling in Engineering, and automate the incident pipeline end to end, including case notes, executive summaries, daily reporting, and retrospectives. Own the security configuration of our corporate stack (identity, endpoint, productivity suite, and secure access), with IT handling day-to-day administration. Own email security (SPF, DKIM, and DMARC), threat and brand intelligence, phishing simulations, and security awareness training. Secure the collaboration AI tools and agents our employees use. Set repeatable standards for credential and secrets management, least-privilege data access, human approval for consequential actions, and audit logging, and maintain an inventory of approved AI tools so the sanctioned path is the easiest one. Track vulnerabilities and threats relevant to Carrot, including attacks on AI systems, and coordinate the response. Set remediation SLAs, report on how well they are met, and manage the annual third-party penetration test through to closure. Support the broader Information Security team on application and product security, third-party vendor risk (with added scrutiny of AI vendors), AI governance, compliance and audit readiness, customer security assessments, privacy partnership with Legal and our Data Protection Officer, and policy and continuity planning. Â What Success Looks Like Â ð In your first 12 months, you will have: Within your first 90 days, taken ownership of incident response and the managed security provider relationship, reviewed detection coverage in our SIEM, built a first inventory of AI tools and agents in use, and identified the biggest gaps in our operational and AI security. Matured incident response with documented runbooks and regular tabletop exercises, with clear communication paths to Legal, Privacy, and executive leadership. Expanded detection coverage and improved alert quality, with measurable gains in time to detect and time to respond. Automated the major steps of the incident pipeline with AI and agents, including investigation, case notes, executive summaries, and daily reporting. Established repeatable standards for AI tool and agent security (credentials, data access, human approval, and audit logging) that partner teams follow. Set vulnerability remediation SLAs, reported on how well they are met, and driven annual penetration test findings to closure. About You â¨ You likely have: 7+ years in security operations, including SIEM-based detection and investigation in a cloud SaaS environment. Experience leading security incidents as incident commander, including executive communication and coordination with Legal. Hands-on experience securing corporate identity, endpoint, and email systems, such as Okta, Google Workspace, and CrowdStrike. Experience managing an MSSP or MDR provider to SLAs. AI fluency: a track record of building security automation with AI or agents, and daily use of AI tools in your own work. The ability to influence partner teams without authority and explain technical risk in business terms. Â Nice to Have â­ While not required, we would be especially excited if you bring: Experience in healthcare or another regulated environment handling PHI or payment data, including HIPAA/HITECH compliance. Experience securing AI agents and integrations, including familiarity with the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications or MITRE ATLAS. Experience with threat or brand intelligence platforms. Familiarity with compliance frameworks (SOC 2, HITRUST, ISO 27001, PCI DSS) and AI risk frameworks (NIST AI RMF, ISO 42001). Certifications such as CISSP, CISM, GIAC, or OSCP. None are required. Â Why This Role Matters ð§¡ Carrot protects some of the most personal information people share: their health, their families, and their path to parenthood. Employers, health plans, and health systems trust us with that responsibility, and that trust depends on a security program that is strong, responsive, and honest about risk. As AI becomes part of how every team works, this role will shape how Carrot adopts it safely. You will build the practices, automation, and partnerships that let us move quickly without putting member data at risk, and you will do it as a hands-on leader whose work is visible across the company. Interview Process ð¤ We believe in a thoughtful and transparent interview process designed to create alignment for both candidates and our team. For this role, candidates can expect: Recruiter Screen â 30 minutes Hiring Manager Interview â 30â45 minutes Technical Interviewâ 60 minutes Team Culture Chatâ 30 minutes Hiring Manager Wrap-Up â 15 minutes Throughout the process, we will share additional context about the team, business priorities, customer landscape, and what success looks like in this role. Â Why Candidates Join Carrot ð Carrot offers the opportunity to do meaningful work in service of a deeply human mission. Highlights include: A mission-driven company focused on expanding access to fertility and family-forming care globally. A high-growth environment where leaders are empowered to shape strategy and drive impact. Competitive compensation, equity, and comprehensive benefits. Flexible Time Off and a culture that actively encourages employees to recharge. Comprehensive parental leave and family-forming benefits. A collaborative, inclusive, and values-driven culture. The opportunity to work alongside passionate, thoughtful teammates committed to improving healthcare outcomes worldwide. Â Compensation Â ð° Carrot offers a holistic Total Rewards package designed to support our employees in all aspects of their life inside and outside of work, including health and wellness benefits, retirement savings plans, short- and long-term incentives, parental leave, family-forming assistance, and a competitive compensation package. The starting base salary for this position will range from $167,000-$185,000. Actual compensation may vary from posted base salary depending on your confirmed job-related skills and experience. Â Fraud and Security Notice: Please note that all communication regarding job opportunities at Carrot will come exclusively from an @get-carrot.com email address. If you receive messages from any other domain, please disregard them and report the incident to: securityreporting@get-carrot.com Â A Note on AI At Carrot, we believe AI can help us work smarter, move faster, and create more meaningful experiences for our members, customers, and each other. While not every role requires deep technical AI expertise, we value people who are curious, eager to learn, and excited to thoughtfully incorporate AI into their day-to-day work. For some roles, AI fluency is a core requirementâand we'll call that out clearly in the qualifications. For everyone else, we're looking for people who embrace new ways of working, use AI responsibly to improve quality and efficiency, and continue to learn as the technology evolves. Why Carrot? Carrot has received national and international recognition for its pioneering work, including Fast Company's Most Innovative Companies and World Changing Ideas, Inc. Power Partners, and Modern Healthcareâs Innovators. Carrotâs global workforce has been acknowledged with several accolades, including Fortuneâs Best Workplaces in Healthcare, Great Place to Work, and Age-Friendly Employer certifications. Carrot is regularly featured in media reporting on issues related to the future of work, women in leadership, and healthcare innovation, including MSNBC, The Economist, Bloomberg, The Wall Street Journal, CNBC, National Public Radio, Harvard Business Review, and more. title: Associate General Counsel, Product
description: ABOUT ABRIDGE Founded in 2018, Abridge is the first AI-native clinician intelligence platform organized around the patient, built for clinicians, and designed to help health systems coordinate the clinical, financial, and evidence-based decisions for every moment of care. Powered by purpose-built AI for healthcare, Abridge connects patients, providers, payers, and life sciences companies. This year, the platform will support more than 100 million patient-clinician conversations across more than 300 of the largest and most complex health systems in the U.S. With deep workflow integration, the Abridge clinician intelligence platform has been validated to support encounters in 28+ languages across specialties and care settings. Abridge is setting the industry standard for the responsible deployment of Al across health systems with continual and transparent Al evaluation. Clinical decision support references and cites gold-standard sources of evidence, and features like Linked Evidence map AI-generated documentation to source data, helping clinicians quickly trust and verify the output. Abridge was awarded Best in KLAS for Ambient AI in 2025 and 2026, in addition to other accolades, including TIME Best Inventions of 2024 and 2025, CNBC Disruptor 2025, and Fast Company’s Most Innovative Companies 2025. We are a growing team of practicing clinicians, AI scientists, PhDs, creatives, technologists, and engineers working together to transform healthcare. We have offices located in San Francisco, New York, and Pittsburgh. THE ROLE As Associate General Counsel, Product, you’ll be a senior legal advisor to the teams building Abridge’s products, focused on our most complex and highest-impact initiatives. You’ll work closely with product and engineering and bring together healthcare, privacy, and AI regulatory requirements with the company’s commercial and operational goals. You’ll help shape how Abridge approaches new legal questions and build the guidance and systems that let teams innovate with confidence. This is a unique opportunity to work at the forefront of AI and healthcare, helping a category-defining company navigate novel legal terrain. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Serve as lead counsel on Abridge’s most complex product initiatives, from early design through launch and post-launch review, including areas where the law is still developing. - Shape the legal strategy for the products and features you support, giving teams practical paths forward that account for regulatory, commercial, and operational realities. - Advise on product launches, feature changes, user-facing disclosures, and marketing claims. - Partner with product, engineering, policy, partner experience, marketing, IT, finance, corporate development, and commercial teams, including senior leadership, to align on risk and move initiatives forward. - Turn recurring issues into practical legal processes, frameworks, and templates that scale with the company. - Provide strategic guidance on regulatory, privacy, and compliance matters, including the evolving AI/ML landscape, and help shape Abridge’s positions on emerging regulation. - Flex across the broader Product, Privacy, and Regulatory Legal portfolio as company priorities and risks change. - Work with outside counsel on specialist issues and turn their advice into fast, actionable guidance for the business. - Monitor emerging laws and regulations affecting Abridge’s products and data practices, and advise stakeholders on their implications. WHAT YOU’LL BRING - Passion for Abridge’s mission and the drive to support fast-moving product and operational teams. - 10+ years of legal experience, including 6+ years in product counseling. Prior in-house experience at a technology company is required. - Experience owning complex, high-stakes legal matters independently, especially where there is little settled precedent. - Sound business judgment and the ability to prioritize risk, balance speed with quality, and know when to bring in specialist expertise. - Proven ability to translate complex regulatory and legal concepts into clear, practical guidance for non-legal colleagues, including senior leaders. - Proven ability to build trusted relationships with technical, design, and commercial teams. - Comfort operating with ambiguity, tight timelines, competing priorities, and a high volume of novel legal questions. - Creativity in solving novel legal problems, including building new processes, language, and frameworks for a fast-moving company in an emerging industry. BONUS POINTS IF… - You have deep expertise in healthcare regulatory matters, including FDA, FTC, fraud, waste, and abuse laws, health data interoperability and/or information blocking rules, and related state laws. - You’re familiar with recent trends in AI, particularly large language models and responsible AI principles. - You have prior experience at a growth-stage, AI-native, or healthcare technology company. LOCATION This role is in our San Francisco
